newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria coalition braces for CA crisis meeting.
newsitem.headline: Austria coalition braces for CA crisis meeting.

text.p: Leaders of Austria's fragile coalition government hold an emergency session on Saturday afternoon in a desperate attempt to restore unity and to iron out differences over who should buy key bank Creditanstalt.

The sale of the government's 70 percent voting stake in 141-year-old Creditanstalt has whipped up a political storm and threatens to derail the fragile alliance of dominant Social Democrats (SPOe) and the conservative People's Party (OeVP).
The SPOe wants Creditanstalt to be sold to Bank Austria, which is effectively controlled by the Social Democrat-led City of Vienna.
The OeVP, together with Creditanstalt's management, favour an international consortium led by insurer EA-Generali.
The unfancied third bid comes from the Wlaschek foundation of retail magnate Karl Wlaschek.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima, a Social Democrat, said he would reveal the winner of the seven-year fight for control of Creditanstalt before Tuesday, when parliament is due to hold a special session on the politically contentious sale.
The minister's deadline for improved bids from the three bidders expired on Friday, when both Bank Austria and the consortium topped up their original offers.
Klima has repeatedly stressed that he is bound by Austrian and European Union law to sell the state's stake of 19.9 million ordinary voting shares to the highest offer.
Bank Austria remains the frontrunner after it raised its offer to 17.2 billion schillings ($1.55 billion) from 16.7 billion, daily Der Standard said on Saturday.
The EA-Generali consortium also raised its bid but trails far behind Bank Austria at 15.1 billion schillings, the paper said. The group originally bid 13.8 billion.
No one in the Finance Ministry was immediately available to confirm the figures.
Wlaschek has stuck to his initial offer, estimated at 15 billion schillings.

In a fresh development on Saturday, the Finance Ministry said a member of the EA-Generali consortium had significantly raised its stake in the group, while the other members had marginally reduced their share.
Sources close to the privatisation told Reuters that Beteiligungsverwaltungs GmbH was the only one of the consortium's 31 members to have raised its share significantly.

According to these sources, it is presumed that financial holding company Beteiligungsverwaltungs GmbH is made up of the three regional Creditanstalt banks -- BKS, Oberbank and BTV -- which officially left the consortium last November.
The Beteiligungsverwaltungs GmbH originally held a 0.9 percent stake in the consortium. ($1=11.09 Schilling)
